title: Who is Markus Lacanilao, the new MARINA administrator?
summary: A public transport group opposes the leadership change in the LTO, citing improvements made during Lacanilao's tenure. Noreen Bernadette San Luis succeeded him as LTO chief.

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has appointed Markus Lacanilao as transportation undersecretary and new head of the Maritime Industry Authority (MARINA).
On Wednesday, November 25, Lacanilao took his oath before Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon.
Dizon said Lacanilao was tasked to modernize MARINA and enforce strict regulations on vessels not following safety regulations

Before being appointed as MARINA administrator, Lacanilao led the Land Transportation Office (LTO) for a little over a year. During his time in LTO, he was a supporter of anti-corruption policies, as well as a proponent of the 7-Point Priority Framework, which discouraged corruption in the agency. He also promoted the digitalization of the agency with the LTO-IT system.

Lacanilao served as special envoy on transnational crime and accompanied former president Rodrigo Duterte to The Hague following his arrest in March 2025. After this, he was appointed as LTO chief in October 2025.
Lacanilao previously served as an assistant secretary at the Office of Civil Defense.

During a Senate inquiry on former president Duterte’s arrest, Lacanilao was briefly detained by the Senate – he was cited for contempt by Senator Imee Marcos because of his supposed conflicting personal accounts. He was later freed after then-Senate president Chiz Escudero said Senator Marcos did not follow proper procedure.
There’s no available public information about Lacanilao’s educational background. In one of the hearings in the Senate, however, he was identified as a civil engineer.
Transport group MANIBELA opposed the leadership change in the LTO. They even held a transport strike from Monday, November 23, until Wednesday, November 25.

The group wanted Lacanilao to remain in his post, pointing out the reforms made under his term such as easier vehicle registration, stricter disciplinary measures against officials, improved delivery of services, among others.

Lawyer and registered nurse Noreen Bernadette San Luis took over Lacanilao’s post in the LTO. San Luis previously served as LTO regional director for Bicol and Calabarzon, as well as director of the LTO Traffic Adjudication Service. – Rappler.com

Zara Pineda is a Rappler volunteer and third-year AB Literature student majoring in Creative Writing and minoring in Commercial Regulations at De La Salle University. She also serves as editor of The LaSallian.
